title: 4521-ESP-ANC-00-60-N185 Field applied paint
summary:
- This document outlines specifications for field applied paint on a project named Solana.
- It includes notices regarding alternate billing cycles, extended payment provisions, and certification periods.
- The scope covers surface preparation and application of coatings and paint in the field.
- General requirements include proper material delivery, storage, labor provision, and adherence to codes.
- Certain materials are excluded from painting, such as Alloy 20, aluminum, lead, and stainless steel.
- Painting operations must be directed by a Construction Superintendent for safety and project coordination.
- Contract allows alternate billing cycles, extended payment, and certification/approval periods.
- Painting should not be done in adverse weather conditions or on wet surfaces.
- Surface preparation varies for different materials (carbon steel, stainless steel, etc.).
- Special care required when cleaning and applying coatings to stainless steel surfaces.
- Uncoated carbon steel surfaces must be prepared according to paint standards.
- Pre-painted steel requires cleaning of abrasions and heat-affected zones before painting.
summary_points: This document outlines specifications for field applied paint on a project named Solana.
It includes notices regarding alternate billing cycles, extended payment provisions, and certification periods.
The scope covers surface preparation and application of coatings and paint in the field.
General requirements include proper material delivery, storage, labor provision, and adherence to codes.
Certain materials are excluded from painting, such as Alloy 20, aluminum, lead, and stainless steel.
Painting operations must be directed by a Construction Superintendent for safety and project coordination.
Contract allows alternate billing cycles, extended payment, and certification/approval periods.
Painting should not be done in adverse weather conditions or on wet surfaces.
Surface preparation varies for different materials (carbon steel, stainless steel, etc.).
Special care required when cleaning and applying coatings to stainless steel surfaces.
Uncoated carbon steel surfaces must be prepared according to paint standards.
Pre-painted steel requires cleaning of abrasions and heat-affected zones before painting.
Epoxy primer must be sealed within one year or brushed blasted for proper application.
Inorganic zinc primer may require high-pressure washing before applying seal coat.
High-temperature paint surfaces remain soft until cured, requiring brush blasting for touch-up.
Contract allows alternate billing cycles other than thirty days.
Owner can request payment within 180 days after certification and approval of billings and estimates.
Owner can certify and approve billings and estimates within 30 days after receipt.
Information is confidential and proprietary to Abener.
Mist coat requires surface preparation by solvent cleaning, air blast, or brush blast.
Paint application must be done on the same day as surface preparation.
Touch-up painting required for damaged areas in shop-painted items.
Shop-primed surfaces require cleaning before applying seal coat.
All painting procedures governed by paint manufacturer's instructions and SSPC-PA-1-64.
Quality control includes visual examination of surface preparation.
Owner can request payment within 180 days after certification and approval.
Owner can certify and approve billings and estimates within 30 days.
Painted surfaces must meet film thickness specifications and visual quality standards.
Defective work must be corrected promptly by the contractor.
Final touch-up is required before leaving the job site.
Surface preparation should comply with Section 3 of this specification.
